question: Do I have to ask customers for permission before sending them promotional emails under this Act?
answer: Not yet as a current duty under this Act: its main duties start on 13 May 2027. The retrieved text does not settle whether promotional emails specifically require prior permission once those duties begin.
details: The Act’s consent provisions are among the provisions scheduled to start on 13 May 2027.
The cited example concerns bill emails, not promotional emails; it says processing for that purpose must cease when the customer opts to receive bills only through the app.
uncertainty: The retrieved passages do not establish whether the Act will require prior permission specifically for promotional emails, or address any requirements under other laws.

notes: Statement 1: The start date is supported, but the STATUS does not address whether promotional emails require prior permission.
Statement 2: Sections 6(1)–(8) and (10) start then, but section 6(9) starts on 13 November 2026.

citations.label: Act No. 22 of 2023, p. 6
citations.quote: The Data Principal may give, manage, review or withdraw her consent to the Data Fiduciary through a Consent Manager. … X shall itself cease, and shall cause Y to cease, the processing of the personal data of Z for emailing bills.
